items.title: Tom Varner interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, August 13, 2025
items.q: And Stan stopped the band and said, “This is not Count Basie.”

ctx.x: That was Al Porcino in the late ‘80s probably.

Yes. Eddie Bert was on the band and he said there was one gig where they were really crowded on the stage, incredibly crowded. And for some reason because of that it felt great and they started swinging. And Stan stopped the band and said, “This is not Count Basie.”

Oh. Terrible. Terrible. Which reminds me of, okay one more, and then we’ve both got to go. Glen Ferris, who is a fantastic trombone player that had played with both Frank Zappa and Harry James, which is hard to imagine, and he’s been in Paris for many years and played with everybody. But when he would really get into a solo he would just move and move and swing, he just couldn’t help it. And at one point Harry James told the lead trombone player or the trumpet player, it’s like, “That kid is pretty good but tell…
